items.text: Here you will find all the insides of the 6 month Fab Academy Program and all the magic that's happening behind!

items.title: What is Digital Fabrication?
items.text: Digital Fabrication refers to the process of producing physical objects derectly from digital designs using computer-controlled tools and machines. It encompasses a wide range od techniques where digital data(such as 3D models or vector files) is transformed into physical items, often through sybtractve, additive, or transformative processes.

items.title: Introduction
items.text:
The idea behind my final project was to create an artistic, interactive piece that actively involves the viewer as part of the experience.

The main idea revolves around Lissajous Curve

items.title: What are Lissajous Curves?
items.text:
A Lissajous curve, also known as a Lissajous figure or Bowditch curve, is the graph of a system of parametric equations:

\[ x = A\sin(at + \delta), \quad y = B\sin(bt) \]

These equations describe the superposition of two perpendicular oscillations in the \(x\) and \(y\) directions with different angular frequencies (\(a\) and \(b\)).

The resulting family of curves was investigated by Nathaniel Bowditch in 1815, and later in more detail in 1857 by Jules Antoine Lissajous (after whom it was named). Such motions may be considered a particular kind of complex harmonic motion.

The appearance of the figure is highly sensitive to the ratio \(\frac{a}{b}\):

  • Ratio of 1 (\(a = b\)): The figure is an ellipse, with special cases including circles (\(A = B, \delta = \frac{\pi}{2}\)) and straight lines (when the phase shift is any multiple of \(\pi\) radians: \(\delta = n\pi, n \in \mathbb{N}\)).
  • Slight frequency change: The \(x\) oscillation after one cycle will be slightly out of synchronization with the \(y\) motion. As a result, the ellipse fails to close and traces a slightly adjacent curve during the next orbit, appearing as a precession of the ellipse.
  • Rational ratio (\(\frac{a}{b}\) is a whole number ratio): The pattern closes completely.

(Sources: Wikipedia – Lissajous Curve, Springer – Foundations of Science)

Lissajous curves in relation to the frequency ratio a/b and phase shift δ.

items.title: Artistic Inspiration
items.text: Lissajous curves are widely used in graphic design, kinetic art installations, and even in cinematography. A famous example is the iconic title sequence of Alfred Hitchcock's movie Vertigo (1958), designed by Saul Bass and John Whitney, where parametric curves were used to create hypnotic visual effects.

items.title: My Project
items.text: For my final project, I aim to visualize Lissajous curves using the classic optical experiment of a laser beam reflecting off two spinning mirrors. To make the installation interactive, the system incorporates motion sensors that detect the observer's presence or movement, dynamically altering the rotational speed of the mirrors and transforming the projected patterns in real time.

items.title: How It Works
items.text:
The optical and mechanical setup operates as follows:

  1. Beam Reflection: A laser beam is directed onto a primary spinning mirror, which then reflects the beam onto a second spinning mirror positioned across from it.
  2. Projection: The combined angular velocities of the two slightly tilted mirrors deflect the laser beam along both the \(x\) and \(y\) axes, projecting complex Lissajous figures onto an adjacent wall.
  3. Interactive Control: Motion sensors mounted along the edge of the base detect the viewer's proximity and movement, feeding data to the microcontroller to modulate the speed of the motors—continuously shifting the frequency ratio and morphing the curve.

items.title: Physical Enclosure
items.text:
The entire optical assembly will be mounted on top of a custom-designed enclosure (box):

  • Top Surface: Houses the laser module and the two motor-driven mirror mounts.
  • Outer Edge: Integrates the motion sensors facing the viewer.
  • Interior: Conceals and protects the custom PCB, motor drivers, wiring, and battery pack.

items.title: Principles and Practices, Project Management
items.text:
The first week of lectures focused on Project Management and how to effectively organize our workflow throughout the program.

Having some previous experience with GitLab, GitHub, and terminal commands gave me a good head start in setting up my workspace.

items.title: Website
items.text:
To start initializing my documentation page, I created a new repository on GitHub to host the website. After setting up the repository, I signed into GitHub directly through Visual Studio Code to connect the two, cloned the repository locally, and began working on it.

Using the integrated VS Code terminal, I created a Python virtual environment to isolate and install the required libraries. Specifically, I ran the following commands:

python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install zensical
zensical new .
After creating your page, you can start your page with 
zensical new
You can view the page on localhost:8000

items.title: Computer Aided Design
items.text: Second week was an indroduction to Computer Aided Design and dedigning in 2D and 3D. It was a topic completely new for me but found really interesting to be able to visualize in a computer objects that suround us.

items.title: Inkscape
items.text:
For 2D design I experimented with Inkscape. After easily downloading it from Microsoft Store, I started following a few tutorials on Youtube to get an idea. (Youtube Links: Inkscape Tutorial) After trying on the designs on the video, I designed something that could be used on my project. Since I will be using laser, even tho it's the most common laser yoy can find, I thought of making a Warning Laser sign that you can see on the picture.

For Vinyl Cutting there is an extension called InkCut

items.title: Tips for Inkscape
items.text:
• Parallelogram + Ctrl -> Square
  • Parallelogram + Ctrl + Shift -> Centered Parallelogram
  • Shift + center of the box -> Center back in the middle
  • Spacebar + object -> copies of object

items.title: Notes on the Logo
items.text:
• When trying to center to triangles together, Inkscape will center them based on the center of the box surrounding them and not the actual center. To center all 3 of the triangles I used, I created the first one and then I made the other 2 using offset.After thta you have to click on Path-> Object to Path for the 2 triangles and you can use them normally.
  • To make them have rounded edges you need to go to Path-> Path Effects-> Corners

items.title: Fushion 360
items.text: For 3D design I decided to use Fushion 360. Since I already had a student account on Autocad from my home university it was only easy to download Fusion 360. I was happily surprised that Fusion was really use to use and had a lot of different tools that make your life easy. To start getting a grasp of it I followed playlist tutorial on Youtube that was guiding you through in detail in designing many basic objects usuing all the tools. The link for the playlist is the following: Fushion 360 Beginner Tutorial. I followed along till Day 15. Tip: Try to make the objects on your own cause it turns out it's easy to forget :)

items.title: Tips on Fushion
items.text:
• Carefully to the construction lines
  • History bar is really important

items.title: Final Project: 2D & 3D
items.text:
For my final project I wanted to make a box. The box will be used to store inside the power supplies(batteries), the motors and the PCB. On the top side of the box there will be the laser, the mirrors and the motion sensors.

To start bulding the box I experimented on some designs from Youtube to learn how to make dovetail joints (Dovetail Joints)

Then combining the dovetail joints with the Finger Joint Box tutorial (Finger Joints), I created a box that has dovetail joints on the side panels for the best stability and finger joints to connect the bottom side. The Top Panel also has an inner rim to connect seamlesssly with the rest of the body.

items.title: Computer Controlled Cutting
items.text: In this week's assignment, we got introduced to Computer Controlled Cutting.

items.title: Parametric Design
items.text:
A Parametric design is a really powerfull method in design. You stop working with precise dimension and you introduce parameters. So every time you want to change one dimension you simple chnage the parameter and everything fits accordigly.

To experiment with parametric design, i designed all of my final project box using parameters. In fushion you can do that by clicking Change Parameters

items.title: Costruction Kit
items.text:
To test the parametric design and the joints I designed a hexagon and a polygon with finger joints. The joints also have camfered edjes. All the dimensions are parameters.

The sketches were exported in .DXF format and imported in Inkscape to be ready to be used in the laser cut.

Note on Kerf Compensation: Kerf is the width of material burned away by the laser beam during cutting (typically around 0.12–0.15 mm). Because this material is removed from both sides of the cut path, a slot drawn at the exact material thickness (4.00 mm) will end up slightly wider, resulting in a loose fit. To achieve a tight press-fit joint without glue, the slot width is parametrically defined as slot_w = t - kerf (3.85 mm), compensating for the laser beam's width.

items.title: Computer Aided Manufacturing(CAM)
items.text: CAM Software: Is a software that takes digital design and converts it into machine instructions. You design ypur part, then you go through the software and through this software you generate the job the machine will execyte afterwards.

items.title: Laser Cutting / Vinyl Cutting
items.text:
Laser Cutting: fast, easy, and accurate way to cut and engrave detailed artwork. To do this, it continuously shoots a powerful laser beam, through series of mirrors and lenses that move laterally and onto a flat bed where sheets of material such as cardboard, MDF and aacrylic are placed

*Generally takes in input 2D files, either vector, raster or both *Generates 2D toolpaths *Considers for lasers: power, speed, freq, job position, focus etc *Considers for Vinyl Cutter: force(downward weight applied to the blade, low for thin material- high for heavy dense materials), speed (how fast the machine moves), cut depth(how much the blade will protrude from the head) , job position etc

!IMPORTANT! You can assign colors to the setting(ex. engrave, cut etc). You cut from inside out. First you do the work inside and last the outside.

Dipnest: Software that put the pieces together to save material

Vinly Cytting Softwares: InkCut, Silhouette Studio
